stem: Which word or phrase correctly connects these two sentences?
stimulus: Bottlenose dolphins in warm coastal waters usually live in pods of a dozen or more animals, hunting and resting together throughout the year. Adult male sperm whales in the open ocean, ______, typically travel alone, joining other whales only briefly during the breeding season.
explanation: Name the subject and attribute of each sentence. The first is about dolphins, which live in groups. The second is about male sperm whales, which travel alone. The two subjects are different and the attribute flips from 'in groups' to 'alone', so you need a contrast word: 'by contrast'. This is the core step in the 'two things set side by side' transition question on the SAT. Spot the shared frame, then check whether the attribute stays the same or flips.

B.why: You saw two sentences with the same frame about sea mammals and assumed they say the same thing. 'Similarly' only works if both animals share the attribute. Here one lives in groups and the other lives alone, so the attribute is reversed.

C.why: You picked 'for example' because a specific animal comes after the blank. An example has to agree with what came before it. Solitary sperm whales don't illustrate group-living dolphins. They are the opposite case.

D.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that isn't there. Dolphins living in pods doesn't make sperm whales travel alone. The two facts are compared, and neither one causes the other.

stem: Which word or phrase correctly connects these two sentences?
stimulus: In many older European cities, streets grew up gradually and still wind in irregular patterns around ancient markets and churches. Many American cities founded in the nineteenth century, ______, were planned in advance on a strict grid of straight, evenly spaced streets.
explanation: The first sentence is about European cities, whose streets are irregular and unplanned. The second is about American cities, whose streets are planned on a grid. The subjects are different and the attribute flips, so 'conversely' is the right link. On the real SAT, this is how you handle a pair of parallel cases where one detail reverses.

A.why: You treated the American cities as a sample of the European ones because a specific group follows the blank. Grid-planned cities can't be an example of winding, unplanned streets. They go against that pattern.

B.why: You noticed both sentences describe city streets and stopped there. 'Likewise' needs the same attribute in both sentences. Irregular streets and a strict grid are opposites.

D.why: You read the second sentence as a conclusion from the first. Winding European streets aren't the reason American cities used grids. The sentences set two cases side by side, and neither causes the other.

stem: Which word or phrase correctly connects these two sentences?
stimulus: Water-soluble vitamins, such as vitamin C and most B vitamins, are not stored in large amounts, so any excess is flushed from the body within a day or two. Fat-soluble vitamins, ______, can build up in the liver and fatty tissue, where the body stores them for months.
explanation: The subjects are water-soluble vitamins and fat-soluble vitamins, and the attribute is whether the body stores them. The first kind is not stored and is flushed out quickly. The second kind is stored for months. Different subjects with an attribute that flips need 'by contrast'. You'll make this same move on SAT transition questions that compare two categories.

A.why: You treated the second sentence as one more fact in the same direction. Try putting 'and also' between the sentences: it sounds wrong, because stored for months reverses not stored. That makes this a contrast, not an addition.

B.why: You reached for 'for example' because a named type of vitamin follows the blank. Fat-soluble vitamins aren't a case of water-soluble vitamins, and they behave the opposite way. An example has to agree with the first claim.

C.why: You assumed the first fact explains the second. How the body handles water-soluble vitamins doesn't cause fat-soluble vitamins to be stored. The sentences are compared, not linked as cause and effect.

stem: Which word or phrase correctly connects these two sentences?
stimulus: Venus spins on its axis so slowly that a single day there lasts longer than its entire year. The giant planet Jupiter, ______, spins faster than any other planet in the solar system, completing a full rotation in under ten hours.
explanation: The first sentence is about Venus, which spins very slowly. The second is about Jupiter, which spins faster than any other planet. The subjects are different and the attribute flips from slowest-type to fastest, so 'conversely' fits. This is the comparison you make on SAT transition questions that set two cases side by side.

A.why: You saw that both sentences describe how a planet spins and treated them as matching. 'Likewise' needs the same attribute. A very slow spin and the fastest spin in the solar system are opposites.

C.why: You picked 'for instance' because one specific planet follows the blank. Jupiter's fast spin doesn't illustrate Venus's slow spin. It goes the other way, so this is a contrast, not an example.

D.why: You read the sentences as steps in a sequence. 'Finally' marks the last item in a list or process. Here nothing is being listed: two planets are being compared.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most of the trees that ring Lake Merrow are deciduous: maples, birches, and oaks drop their leaves each autumn and stand bare until spring. The white pines along the lake's western shore, ______, hold on to their needles through the winter and stay green even under heavy snow.
explanation: This is groundwork for the 'two things set side by side' transition question. Cover the choices and name the two subjects and what each one does. In the first sentence, most of the lake's trees drop their leaves and stand bare. In the second, the white pines keep their needles and stay green. The subjects differ and the attributes are opposites (bare vs. green), so you need a comparison-contrast word. 'By contrast' is that word. On the real test, the blank often sits mid-sentence, set off by commas, just as it does here.

A.why: You saw a specific kind of tree come after a general statement about 'most of the trees' and assumed it was an example. An example has to agree with the general claim, though, and the pines do the opposite: they stay green while the others go bare. A specific case that breaks the pattern is a contrast, not an illustration. Before you pick 'for example', always check that the case actually fits the rule.

B.why: 'Similarly' needs both subjects to share the same attribute. That would only work if the pines also dropped their leaves. Here one group goes bare and the other stays green, so the attributes are opposites, not matches.

D.why: 'As a result' says the first sentence caused the second. The maples and oaks losing their leaves doesn't make the pines keep their needles. The two sentences describe different trees side by side, and neither causes the other.
